description.describe_ch: This course is an introduction to physics. The main emphasis will be on the branch of physics known as mechanics. This is the study of motion and the causes of motion through the applications of fundamental principles of physics. We begin with kinematics, the quantitative description of the motion of particles. We then build on kinematics to learn how and why motion occurs, through the application of  Newton's laws of dynamics. Many examples will be considered as we explore the properties of specific forces and the details of the motion they bring about. The next step will be to describe physical processes in terms of energy and momentum, quantities that are always "conserved." Conservation laws allow us to solve problems in mechanics that would be very difficult by other techniques and provide a powerful approach to the analysis of physical systems in general. We then will extend our understanding of motion to the kinematics and dynamics of rotation. Finally, we will briefly study some of the physical properties of solids and fluids.

textBooks.tpb_book_en:
Any introductory physics textbook (regardless of author or edition) can serve as the textbook for this course.
Students can either buy a textbook from the local bookstores or borrow one from friends.
The one commonly used for FCU freshmen is shown below:  
Douglas Giancoli's "Physics for Scientists and Engineers with Mordern Physics"
2023 (5th ed/ Global Edition) Volume 1 (Pearson)
Taiwan's dealer：東華書局/新月圖書，台中市北屯區旱溪東路三段38號，TEL (04)2285-5820, Cell Phone 0952-135332

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new_en:

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
All course activities will be carried out in an atmosphere of friendly participation and interaction among students, respecting and appreciating
each student's personal experience, background and perspectives, such as various school systems at home and abroad, diverse enrollment and
learning cultures, gender, etc. You are expected to apply the highest academic standards throughout this course and to treat fellow students with
dignity and respect.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en:
Students are welcome to contact the instructors through either the face-to-face comunications or the e-mail (yinglee@o365.fcu.edu.tw)
The instructor will approve students' requesting for class leave as long as the supporting document (in either photo or image format) is attached
and fullfills one of the following situations：  
1. It is not needed according to the related university regulations. 
2. It is provided by the clinics or hospitals and it shows the student's name as well as the date of visiting. 
3. It is provided by the departments of university or government for manatory events (such as the military service medical examination), and it
shows the student's name and the related date.
4. It is a memo with a brief description of the event and it MUST be signed by one of the following persons:
students' parents or guardians, the full-time prodessor of the department that the student belongs to.
* A personal photo, a photo of the medicine bag or clinic buildings, a note without signatures from the person aforementioned...etc will not be
accpeted as the supporting document.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
Learning must be based on honesty. Any student who attempts to use a work that he has not produced as his own is considered
dishonest.Students who cheat or plagiarize in homework, tests or exams, or assist others, will be scored as zero. If they are repeat offenders, they
will besubmitted in accordance with the rewards and punishments for students of Feng Chia University.
